reason: Same mechanism: predictable institutional month-end flows (pension/60-40 rebalancing) pressuring SPY vs IEF in the last days of the month, same instruments and dev period. Only the direction rule differs (always long equity in the window vs sign of month-to-date drift). Merging makes the multiple-testing penalty stricter, the safe direction.

H-0029 sorts LIQ-500 stocks on the same past-month return as the reversal trials (study 5, H-0007, H-0030, H-0006) and trades its sign, only conditioned on turnover. It tests the same cross-section with the opposite sign, so the trials are one question; separate names would hide them from the multiple-testing count. Merging only makes the penalty stricter. K-0044 already treats these as one claim.

H-0037 is registered as liquidity_provision like H-0006, H-0030 and H-0035: it fades a recent relative price deviation over a few sessions and is paid by whoever pushed the price away. The wrapper/AP-arbitrage story could not be tested, because the catalog holds no NAV or intraday premium, only daily closes of two wrappers, so what was actually run is a daily deviation fade. It died the same way against cost, with the same early-era pattern (K-0052). The Librarian's lesson says not to call another daily fade of a recent deviation a new mechanism without wrapper evidence, and there is none. Counting the trial together is the stricter direction. If wrapper-level data (price against NAV) ever exists, a new card can argue the AP mechanism, but its trials would still count here.
